fourth_pass_blockers.issue_3_panels_missed: Compositional Bash-pattern self-block: T1.2 guardrails patterns `\bUPDATE\s+\w+\s+SET\b`, `\bDELETE\s+FROM\s+\w+`, `\bINSERT\s+INTO\b`, `\bTRUNCATE\b` apply to Bash matcher `*`. This blocks the executor's OWN required operations: (a) `~/scripts/exec-state.sh` runs `jq` mutations that the script body never shows but jq filters with words `update/delete` may match in command line tokens; (b) ANY `psql ... -c "UPDATE schema_migrations ..."` legitimate migration ops (cicatrix scar 2026-04-29 migration 146 trigger contains `INSERT INTO events_outbox`); (c) `git commit -m "... UPDATE memory ..."` arbitrary commit messages now blocked because regex matches inside `-m "..."` string; (d) `/scar` command (T3.4) writes scar text that may itself contain `UPDATE` / `INSERT` as English words → guardrails kills the write. The 3 panels added each pattern independently and never re-tested the cumulative pattern set against typical Bali Zero operational Bash usage.
fourth_pass_blockers.fix: Restrict SQL patterns to `Bash(psql|sqlite3) command-line position ONLY` via anchored regex `^\s*(psql|sqlite3)\b.*-c\s+['\"](DROP|UPDATE|DELETE|INSERT|TRUNCATE)` AND remove them from generic Bash matcher; move SQL-content enforcement to dedicated wrapper script `~/scripts/safe-psql.sh` invoked by guidelines. For .sql files, keep the file-content check but exempt SAFE migration patterns (UP/DOWN canonical Alembic format) via a whitelist regex.

fourth_pass_blockers.issue_3_panels_missed: Self-termination paradox: `pkill -KILL -f "claude"` (line 1220) is invoked from a script that is itself executed BY the Claude Code session being killed. Bash subshell launched by Claude's Bash tool inherits the parent's process group; pkill matches `claude` substring which catches `claude-acct2`, `claude-stop-drain.sh`, `claude-pg-...` scripts AND the parent claude process. Result: Bash command termination mid-flight, partial rollback state, safety backup may not finish writing, settings.json moved aside but new state not restored. Gemini panel noted WAL safety but missed that the kill mechanism cannot work from inside the very process being killed. GPT-5.5 panel reviewed exit codes but not process tree.
fourth_pass_blockers.fix: G3 must be invoked from OUTSIDE Claude Code (Antonello terminal). Add hard precondition in script preamble: `[ -n "$CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN" ] && { echo "ERROR: G3 must run from external terminal, not from inside Claude Code session"; exit 1; }` — use any Claude-session-only env var as canary. Alternative: G3 schedules itself via `at now+1min` after capturing Claude PIDs explicitly, then exits — `at` job runs after Claude is gone.

fourth_pass_blockers.spec: T1.1 dispatch_nudge + T2.5 PreCompact + T2.6 stop_verify
fourth_pass_blockers.issue_3_panels_missed: Cumulative O(N) transcript scan on EVERY user prompt: T1.1 reads full transcript (`p.read_text()`), T2.5 parses last 2000 events (writes to disk), T2.6 reads last 10KB. On an 18.5K-line Karpathy-baseline session (CLAUDE.md cites this), transcript file is 5-15MB. T1.1 reads ENTIRE file then slices last 40KB — but `read_text()` loads ALL into RAM. At 200 user prompts/session, that's 200×(5-15MB) reads = 1-3GB of I/O during single dense session. Python startup + read_text + count operations = 200-800ms latency added to EVERY UserPromptSubmit. Hook timeout is 3000ms; remaining budget for other UserPromptSubmit hooks (settings.json already has 3) dwindles. Combined with PreCompact hook (8s timeout) and Stop hook (10s timeout), cumulative I/O budget across hooks during one session ≈ 5-10× the I/O of unrigged Claude Code. 3 panels reviewed timeout values but not aggregate hook-induced I/O on dense sessions.
fourth_pass_blockers.fix: T1.1 must use `os.path.getsize` + `seek(file_size - RECENT_BYTES)` + `read(RECENT_BYTES)` instead of read_text(). Same fix for T2.5 (use tail-N parser, not full slurp). Add transcript-size guard: if file > 50MB, sample 3 windows (start, middle, end) of 40KB each instead of slurping. Document cumulative hook latency budget in T3.5 (sum of all timeouts × frequency).

fourth_pass_blockers.spec: All settings.json mutations (T1.1, T1.2, T2.5, T2.6 wire + rollback blocks)
fourth_pass_blockers.issue_3_panels_missed: Non-atomic settings.json mutations: every wire-in/rollback block uses `p.write_text(json.dumps(s, indent=2))` directly on `~/.claude/settings.json`. This is NOT atomic on macOS — if Claude Code process reads the file mid-write (SessionStart, hook reload), it sees truncated/invalid JSON and either crashes hooks or runs with ZERO hooks (silent guardrails bypass!). Worse: settings.json is read by Claude harness on every hook invocation (per Anthropic spec). T-1 backup snapshot may catch a corrupt settings.json that was rolled-back-to. Three panels added MORE write-points without considering write atomicity. Also there's no schema validator — a typo in patterns array breaks parsing, hooks silently disabled.
fourth_pass_blockers.fix: Replace direct `p.write_text(...)` with: `tmp = p.with_suffix('.json.tmp.NEW'); tmp.write_text(...); tmp.rename(p)` (POSIX-atomic rename on same filesystem). Add `jq empty <new>` validation BEFORE rename. Add post-write schema sanity check: count of hooks before/after must match expected delta. Add file lock (`fcntl.flock`) wrapping the read-modify-write sequence to prevent concurrent T1.1+T1.2+T2.5 hook installs from race-corrupting.

fourth_pass_blockers.issue_3_panels_missed: Manifest mutation race + jq tmp+mv NOT cross-wave-safe: T-2 uses `jq '...' "$MANIFEST" > "$MANIFEST.tmp" && mv "$MANIFEST.tmp" "$MANIFEST"`. If two Wave executors run concurrently (e.g., Wave 2 install scripts can fire parallel: T2.2 Playwright + T2.3 GitHub + T2.4 Vercel all do `claude mcp add`), the last `mv` wins and silently overwrites completed work of the other. Resulting manifest claims fewer specs done than reality → re-execution duplicates installs → MCP registry double-registers → undefined behavior. Worse: the `next` selector uses sort order assuming sequential execution; concurrent dispatch returns same `next` to multiple workers. Gemini panel created T-2 to survive compaction but missed concurrency. GPT-5.5 reviewed the jq query but not concurrency.
fourth_pass_blockers.fix: Add flock around exec-state mutations: `( flock -x 200; jq ... > $MANIFEST.tmp; mv $MANIFEST.tmp $MANIFEST ) 200>$MANIFEST.lock`. Document that Wave executors MUST be serial within a wave (not parallel) until manifest gains true CAS semantics. Add hash-fingerprint to detect lost-update: each `start` and `done` reads current sha256 of manifest and writes new sha256; if mid-flight sha256 changed → abort + alert.

T1.1 + T2.5 + T2.6 all read transcript on hook fire. UserPromptSubmit fires N times/session (where N = user prompts). PreCompact fires 1x/session. Stop fires 1x/session. Cumulative I/O on 50MB transcript = 200×50MB reads from T1.1 alone = 10GB sequential reads/session. SSD wear + ~30s aggregate latency overhead/session.

T1.2 guardrails fires on EVERY tool call (matcher=*). Python startup ~50ms × tool calls per session. Dense Bali Zero session has 200-500 tool calls = 10-25s aggregate Python startup overhead. Anti-pattern: should use long-lived hook daemon, not subprocess invocation per call.

Last 2000 events = 20-100MB read AT compaction time, during the 8s timeout — this may exceed timeout under disk pressure or large outputs. If T-1 runs with <500MB free (cicatrix scar 2026-05-14 'disk full' precedent), tarball is corrupt, manifest written, executor proceeds thinking backup is good → G3 rollback later finds corrupt tar → unrecoverable.

Telegram bot token rotation mid-execution: T-1 inventory captures Keychain item NAMES, not values. If Antonello rotates TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN between T-1 (Wave 0 start) and G3 rollback execution (Wave 3 failure 6h later), G3's Phase 6 telegram alert uses environment token which may be invalid → operator never notified of rollback completion.

claude CLI subprocess inside hook subprocess: T2.5 hook is python3 subprocess. T1.4 karpathy-discipline skill body may call `claude` CLI (Codex spalla pattern). Nested claude invocations spawned from inside a hook fired from a parent claude session = OAuth slot contention. Cicatrix MEMORY.md notes 'slot 1 default, slot 2 via claude-acct2' — but hooks don't know which slot to use, default = slot 1 = same as parent = quota race.

Git clean -fd in G3 Phase 4 line 1357: `git clean -fd -e ".env*" -e "*.local"` runs AFTER `git reset --hard <tag>`. If reset succeeded, working tree matches tag — nothing untracked. But if executor created files (research capture, scar, etc.) BEFORE running G3, those files are 'untracked' and `git clean -fd` DELETES them. The `-e` exclusions only cover .env*. Research captures in research/operations/specs/ that aren't in the tag get nuked. Single-cmd rollback also nukes documentation of WHY we rolled back.

G4 weekly cron + Pro/Mini topology: G4 monitors orchestration health via `find SESSION_DIR -mtime -7`. Pro sessions live on Pro disk only; Mini sessions on Mini. G4 runs on Pro per spec — Mini work invisible. If T2.5 PreCompact handoffs accumulate on Mini (Mode B companion), G4 reports 'no sessions' falsely.

Empty TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN env var: G2's plist (line 1041) has `<key>TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN</key><string></string>` — empty placeholder. Plist as-loaded passes empty string to script which evaluates `[ -n "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN:-}" ]` = false → telegram silently skipped → operator never alerted to validation results. The 'optional cron' becomes 'silent fail'.

Hook timeout cascade silently disabled: Claude harness defaults to fail-open on hook timeout per Anthropic spec. If T1.2 guardrails hits 3000ms timeout (Python cold start + transcript I/O), Claude harness ALLOWS the tool call to proceed. So under sustained CPU pressure, guardrails effectively disables itself — most destructive operations would be the ones putting CPU under pressure (rm -rf large dir, dd, etc.). Inverse of antifragile: load conditions weaken protection.

T0.1 backup tar then DELETE flow: Step 1 creates `~/backups/orphan-triage-20260521.tar.gz`. Step 5 DELETE. Restoration via tar -xzf assumes backup tarball intact. But cicatrix 2026-04-29 documents a 'tar tarball with secrets in plist' attack. Same pattern here: orphan memory files include `api-keys.md` (per spec Open Question #1, may contain secrets). Backup tarball now contains plaintext secret as archive payload at default 0644 mode after tar.
honest_assessment: Plan is procedurally exhaustive — 31 specs with 4-LLM review integration is unusually thorough — but 4th-pass analysis reveals the panels reviewed each spec in isolation and not the COMPOSITIONAL behavior of running them together on a Bali Zero machine. The three panel methodology converged on coverage breadth (matchers, edge cases, secrets handling) but missed dynamics: (1) self-block paradoxes from cumulative pattern matching (guardrails patterns block executor's own ops and documentation), (2) hook-induced I/O at session scale (200 prompts × full-transcript read = GB-scale I/O), (3) non-atomic settings.json writes that race-corrupt under any sibling-agent presence (cicatrix 2026-04-29 already showed this exact attack surface), (4) G3 self-termination paradox (cannot run from inside Claude), (5) concurrent manifest mutations breaking T-2 single-execution assumption. The plan would likely SHIP and APPEAR successful for first ~70% of waves, then degrade silently as load increases. Recommend: add a 'WAVE -1' integration smoke test that exercises 2-3 specs in combination under realistic dense-session conditions (18.5K-line transcript, parallel agent dispatch, mid-execution compaction) BEFORE committing to T-1 backup creation. Lower effort estimate is too optimistic — realistic 20-25h once compositional fixes added. Plan quality is good (B+) but not yet shippable (A-).
